conviction_note: Near non-result: the Q3 step-up from $0.61 to a $0.82-0.85 bar is mostly what the company guided for H2 (Hamilton back on longwall, AllDale III/IV from 1 July). The one item probably not fully in the bar is a ~$16M bitcoin fair-value gain on 646 BTC (BTC +42.7% in Q3) against a $6.3M loss in Q2. That should lift reported EPU but is excluded from adjusted EBITDA and DCF, which are what this MLP trades on. Industry proxies point slightly down: Illinois Basin output fell 6.2% y/y quarter-to-date and utility stockpiles are high, which bears on 2027 contracting. abs_move 4.5 sits between the 3.65 median reaction and the indicative 5.97 implied move. p_up 55 reflects 5 of 7 prior reactions up and a likely headline EPS beat. The findings sum (+0.2) and the scaled number (+0.45) agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 2026 EPU about $0.82-0.85 and revenue about $586-590M. Benzinga consensus $0.82 / $590.0M (27 Aug snapshot; Sidoti $0.82, Noble $0.85), Earnings Whispers $0.84 / $588.8M, Stockalarm revenue average $586M (range $559-613M). Sources: https://es.benzinga.com/quote/ARLP/earnings-forecasts, https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/ARLP, https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/ARLP/analysts. The sources agree within 3 cents, so the bar is treated as sourced. The company's FY2026 guide (coal 33.75-35.25 Mt, $54-56/t, cost $37-39/t) is in the 2026-07-27 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001086600/000110465926086855/arlp-20260727xex99d1.htm. Whether the two to three covering analysts model the bitcoin fair-value line is not known.
positioning_check: Short interest about 1.6M units at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 6.3 days to cover, against 128.66M units outstanding (about 1.2%), within a 2026 range of 1.3-1.7M (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/arlp/short-interest/). Borrow fee 0.4% in a July snapshot. Not a crowded short. The baseline's skew_25d is null. Put/call open interest is 0.21 on only 2,000 contracts total, and the ATM spread is 60% of mid, so the 5.97% event-implied move is indicative only. Run-up is +3.86% over 20 days and +1.44% over 5 days; the stock is 9.9% below its 52-week high.

findings.finding: ARLP held 646 bitcoins worth $37.9M at 30 June 2026 (about $58.7k each) and booked a $6.3M Q2 fair-value loss. Bitcoin closed Q3 up 42.71% at about $83.7k, which implies a Q3 mark-to-market gain of roughly $15-16M if the holding was unchanged. That is a swing of about +$22M (about +$0.17 per unit on 128.66M units) against Q2, on a bar of $0.82-0.85 that rose from $0.78 before the Q2 print. The gain is excluded from adjusted EBITDA and DCF, so it lifts headline EPU only.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 2026 bitcoin fell about 22% (an $11.7M loss) and the stock still rose 2.21% on the print. In Q2 2026, a $6.3M loss, it rose 3.72%. In Q3 2025 a $3.7M gain came with +4.12%. The line has never visibly driven the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar's step from $0.61 to $0.82-0.85 is explained by the guided H2 coal and royalty recovery alone (see the next finding). If the two or three covering analysts had added a ~$0.12-0.17 bitcoin gain, the bar would sit nearer $0.95. With bitcoin up 43%, a stock pricing the gain should have run up more than 3.9% over 20 days. The line sits below operating income and has no path to the guide or the distribution, which is why it is sized as a fraction of the same money earned as operating profit.
findings.independence: Independent price series: Forklog/CoinGlass Q3 close of +42.71% at about $83.7k (https://forklog.com/en/?p=104576) and COINOTAG via edgeX, 2026-10-01 (https://pro.edgex.exchange/en-US/news/article/bitcoin-q3-2026-best-quarter-since-2017). Holding count and value come from the company's Q2 release; the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1086600/000110465926092001/arlp-20260630x10q.htm) reports no post-quarter sale.

findings.finding: The 27 July release says Hamilton is back on longwall production with no further longwall moves until 2027, and 2026 sales are 'essentially fully committed at the midpoint'. H1 sold 16.42 Mt at a segment cost of about $40/t (Q1 $41.42, Q2 $38.68). The guidance midpoint (34.5 Mt, $37-39/t) therefore implies about 9.0 Mt a quarter in H2 at roughly $36-37/t, against Q2's 8.56 Mt and $38.68. This is the improvement the market was told to expect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume and cost recoveries signalled the quarter before were bought modestly: Q2 2026 delivered the signalled sequential volume rise (8.56 vs 7.86 Mt) and the stock rose 3.72%. In October 2025, when Appalachian setbacks cut guidance, the print still rose 4.12%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the Q3 bar rose from $0.78 (24 July) to $0.82 (27 August) after the release, which is the market writing this in. Only the gap between a delivered H2 run-rate and a merely guided one is unpriced, which is why the size is near zero.
findings.independence: Same document as the guidance. Consensus migration is from Benzinga (https://es.benzinga.com/quote/ARLP/earnings-forecasts).

findings.finding: EIA weekly estimates reported by Argus on 10 September 2026 put Illinois Basin output (IL, IN, western KY, where ARLP is a major producer) down 6.2% year on year at about 11.6M st for Q3 to date. US output was down 4.1% over the 10 weeks to 5 September, and EIA forecasts Q3 US production of 130.9M st against 135.9M st in Q3 2025. The bar implies ARLP's Q3 coal volume rising to about 9 Mt, roughly flat to up on Q3 2025's 8.7 Mt.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume shortfalls have been looked through: the Q3 2025 print came with a cut to 2025 sales guidance and the stock rose 4.12%. The Q2 2025 volume and price softness print fell 1.72%.
findings.why_not_priced: Industry weekly production data are not read through to ARLP by its two or three covering analysts, whose bar moved up after July. Had the market read it, the Q3 revenue bar ($586-590M) would sit nearer the Q2 run-rate ($551.6M) rather than up about 7%. The size is small because it is a proxy, and the company's own primary-document statement (2026 essentially fully committed at the midpoint, Hamilton back on longwall) cuts against transmission to ARLP specifically.
findings.independence: Proxy only. A partial weekly data point is consistent: SXCoal citing EIA had Illinois state output down 8.5% y/y in the week to 29 August (https://en.sxcoal.com/news/detail/2095681120576409602). The company's own contracted book points the other way.

findings.finding: S&P Global (15 October 2026) says US coal stockpiles stayed high and constrained domestic price gains in September, and expects elevated 2026 stockpiles to limit demand into 2027. That bears on the 2027 committed and priced tonnage the Q3 release normally updates (29.4 Mt for 2027 at Q2) and on any preliminary 2027 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 prints carry the first read on next year's book. The Q3 2025 print (2025 guidance cut, 2026 contracting update) rose 4.12%. No print in the baseline fell more than 3.83% (Q1 2025, February 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is 9.9% below its 52-week high but up 3.9% over 20 days, which is not the pattern of a market pricing a weaker 2027 book. If 2027 risk were priced, the 2027 committed-tonnage line would not be expected to grow. The size is small because this is a market-level read (snippet only, page 403 to fetch) that the company has not confirmed.
findings.independence: The June/July S&P piece 'Slack demand, surging inventory pressurize US coal prices' points the same way (https://hellenicshippingnews.com/slack-demand-surging-inventory-pressurize-us-coal-prices). The next finding is partly offsetting and comes from the same S&P October document.

findings.finding: Illinois Basin 11,500 mid-sulfur spot rose $0.75 to $54.75/st in September 2026 (S&P Global), above ARLP's Illinois Basin realised $51.87/t in Q2 and its $50-52 guide. EIA describes June-August 2026 as exceptionally hot, with Henry Hub averaging $2.93. This supports pricing on 2027 tons still to be contracted and any spot sales.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pricing commentary on next year's book has accompanied up-moves in 4 of the last 5 prints (2.21% to 4.12%).
findings.why_not_priced: Benchmark-to-company transmission is slow, because ARLP's 2026 book is fixed and 2027 pricing is disclosed only on calls. If the market had priced a firmer IB spot, the 2027 price would already be talked up in previews, and no Q3 2026 preview was found. The size is small for the same proxy reason.
findings.independence: Hot summer and low gas: EIA analysis of 25 September 2026 cited via https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=68204. The spot figure shares a document with the stockpile finding above. The two can both be true: spot is up modestly while stockpiles stay high.

findings.finding: Oil and gas royalty pricing fell in Q3: WTI averaged about $94-95 in Q2 2026 (ARLP realised $49.43/BOE) but about $79 from 1 July to 8 August per the Dallas Fed. The AllDale III/IV acquisition, closed 1 July, adds about 48,500 net royalty acres, raised FY volume guidance, and is consolidated from Q3 with Craft-related entities holding $100M of AllDale III limited partner interests, which raises noncontrolling interest.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A record royalty segment (Q2 2026, $46.3M revenue, +30.5% y/y) came with +3.72%. The segment is about 8% of revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: The oil price is public, and volume is guided, so this is mostly priced. What may not be modelled is the accounting: consolidating AllDale III inflates royalty revenue but shifts part of it to noncontrolling interest. Net of the coal segment (about 85% of revenue) this is a small line.
findings.independence: The consolidation language is in the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1086600/000110465926092001/arlp-20260630x10q.htm). Q2 WTI is also in the Montana tax table (https://revenue.mt.gov/taxes/natural-resource-taxes/crude-oil-prices/).

findings.finding: Q2 distribution coverage was 1.39x ($108.2M DCF), up 39% sequentially. Q3 coverage should rise further on higher H2 cash flow, but management's stated priorities after the $206M AllDale purchase (funded partly by a new $150M term loan) are leverage reduction and disciplined acquisitions, so the $0.60 quarterly distribution is most likely held. A cut is very unlikely; a raise would be an unguided upside tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The distribution has been $0.60 since the Q1 2025 cut from $0.70. That February 2025 print was the worst reaction in the baseline (-3.83%). The four flat-distribution prints since then were +0.63, -1.72, +4.12 and +3.65.
findings.why_not_priced: At a $2.40 annualised yield of about 9.2% on $26.12, the market prices a held distribution. A raise is not in any preview found and would show up as a lower yield. The size is small because management signalled deleveraging first.
findings.independence: Same document. The Quartr Q2 summary repeats the leverage-reduction focus and describes no distribution change (https://quartr.com/events/alliance-resource-partners-lp-arlp-q2-2026_ozmz0e5W).

findings.finding: Insider flow into the print is negligible. Officer Mark A. Watson filed a Form 144 on 15 September 2026 to sell 6,606 units (about $173k) acquired as equity compensation, and director Ronna McDaniel's only Form 4 (18 August) is a 69.74-unit purchase at $25.81, a reinvestment-sized amount. No Form 4 from Craft was found in 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None: insider flow has not been a line this name trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and immaterial. It is filed for completeness because the absence of an insider cluster ahead of the print is itself information.

baseline_tension: There is no skew and a mild +3.9% 20-day run-up. The findings net to a small positive, driven by a below-the-line bitcoin gain, and slight industry-proxy negatives on volume and 2027 demand. Nothing cuts strongly against what the market has priced.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guided range): Hamilton/H2 volume-cost finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1
Rule 5 (proxy vs primary document): Illinois Basin output proxy cut from -0.5 to -0.3, because the company's own release says 2026 is essentially fully committed
Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission unconfirmed): stockpile/2027 finding cut from -0.5 to -0.4 and IB spot/hot summer from +0.3 to +0.2
Rule 2 (one_off sized as a fraction): bitcoin gain already sized as one_off at +0.6 in the draft, left unchanged so the rule is not applied twice
Rule 7: short interest checked (1.2% of units, 6.3 days to cover), not crowded; no skew available; no change
